Substituting x=3 gives 2(3)^3 + m(3)^2 - 13(3) + n = 0 , yielding 9m + n = -15 . Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 5m = -25 , so m = -5 . Substituting into 4m + n = 10 gives 4(-5) + n = 10 , hence n = 30 . Finally, 4m + 5n = 4(-5) + 5(30) = -20 + 150 = 130 . The result is 130 .

71326.text: While describing the dynamics of cell growth, the ratio of change in number of cells over the time interval is called ____.
71326.sol: The absolute growth rate is defined as the measurement and comparison of total growth per unit time. 71464.text: During glycolysis, which one of the following intermediates undergoes oxidation as well as phosphorylation?
71464.sol: During glycolysis, the conversion of 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (3-PGAL) to 1,3-bisphosphoglyceric acid (1,3-BPGA) is catalyzed by the enzyme glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase. In this step, 3-PGAL undergoes oxidation by the removal of hydrogen, which is accepted by NAD⁺ to form NADH + H⁺ . Simultaneously, it undergoes phosphorylation by the addition of inorganic phosphate ( H₃PO₄ ) to form 1,3-BPGA. 71850.subject: Chemistry
71850.text: Identify the type of reaction when benzene reacts with nitrating mixture.
71850.sol: Benzene reacts with a nitrating mixture (a mixture of concentrated HNO₃ and concentrated H₂SO₄ ) to form nitrobenzene. In this process, the nitrating mixture generates the nitronium ion ( NO₂^+ ), which acts as an electrophile. The electrophile attacks the electron-rich benzene ring, replacing one of its hydrogen atoms with a nitro group ( -NO₂ ). Since a hydrogen atom is replaced by another group, this is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction. Answer: Substitution

74011.sol: Things float on the principle of Archimedes’ principle When an object floats on a liquid the buoyant force that acts on the object is equal to the weight of the object. • If the weight of the object is less than the upthrust, then the object will float on the fluid. • If the weight of the object is greater than the upthrust, then the object will sink in the fluid. • If the weight of the object is equal to the upthrust, then the object will float with half of its body immersed.

options: To carry out physical reactions and maintain structural stability
To hold the substrate for a chemical reaction and provide functional groups
To create and destroy chemical bonds
120363.sol: Enzymes perform two major functions: holding the substrate for a chemical reaction and providing functional groups.

120740.subject: Chemistry
120740.text: What is the product of the reaction between glucose and hydrogen cyanide?
120740.sol: Glucose reacts with hydrogen cyanide to give cyanohydrin.

120917.subject: Chemistry
120917.text: What are the important structural and functional differences between DNA and RNA?
options: DNA and RNA have identical structures and functions.
DNA is single-stranded, while RNA is double-stranded. DNA carries genetic information, while RNA is involved i
DNA is double-stranded, while RNA is single-stranded. DNA carries genetic information, while RNA is involved i
DNA and RNA have the same functions but differ in their chemical composition.
120917.sol: Correct Option is : (C) DNA is double-stranded, while RNA is single-stranded. DNA carries genetic information, while RNA is involved in protein synthesis and other cellular functions.

121200.subject: Botany
121200.text: Taxonomic Categories Categories A. Phylum 1. Group comprising all animals B. Division 2. Group comprising all plants C. Kingdom Animalia 3. Group including classes like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals D. Kingdom Plantae 4. Higher category for plants with a few similar characters
121200.sol: Phylum includes classes like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals. Division is the higher category for plants. Kingdom Animalia includes all animals, while Kingdom Plantae includes all plants.

121288.subject: Botany
options: By a primitive type of DNA transfer only
By fission, producing spores, and a primitive type of DNA transfer
121288.sol: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Sometimes, under unfavourable conditions,they produce spores. They also reproduce by a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other.

122105.subject: Botany
122105.text: Which of the given genera is homosporous?
122105.sol: In pteridophytes, majority of plants are homosporous (producing similar kind of spores) e.g., Lycopodium. However, plants of genera like Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous (producing macro and micro spores). Pinus and Cycas, which are gymnosperms, are also heterosporous.

122155.subject: Botany
122155.sol: Polyembryony is of common occurrence among the gymnosperms. This is possible because more than one archegonia are fertilized and more than one zygotes are formed. These develops into embryos, but only one of them succeeds in developing into a complete embryo. In the conifers there is a cleavage polyembryony. In this case all the four cells of the young embryo separate and develop into 4 embryos, but only one completely develop and others abort, eg Pinus.

122253.subject: Botany
122253.text: What is the notochord replaced by in the adult members of Vertebrata subphylum?
122253.sol: The members of subphylum Vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period. The notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. Vertebrates have a ventral muscular heart with two, three or four chambers, kidneys for excretion and osmoregulation and paired appendages which may be fins or limbs.All living members of the class Cyclostomata are ectoparasites on some fishes.Cyclostomes have an elongated body bearing 6-15 pairs of gill slits for respiration.Cyclostomes have a suckin

122525.subject: Botany
122525.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Wuchereria is classified as a true coelomate animal. Reason (R): In Wuchereria, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options give
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
122525.sol: Wuchereria belongs to the phylum Aschelminthes. Members of Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates, not true coelomates. Therefore, the Assertion is false. In pseudocoelomates like Wuchereria, the body cavity is not completely lined by mesoderm. Instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Therefore, the Reason is true. Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true

122743.subject: Botany
122743.text: What is the definition of aestivation?
options: The study of plants and flowers
The study of birds and their habitats
The arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl
122743.sol: The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as aestivation. The main types of aestivation are valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary (Figure 5.11). When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate. If one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on as in china rose, lady’s finger and cotton, it is called twisted. If the margins of sep

122760.subject: Botany
122760.text: In which type of placentation does the placenta develop at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it?
122760.sol: The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as placentation. The placentation are of different types namely, marginal, axile, parietal, basal, central and free central (Figure 5.12). In marginal placentation the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows, as in pea. When the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, the placentaion is said to be axile, as in china rose, tomato and lemon. In parietal

123157.subject: Botany
123157.text: During formation of which of the following free nuclear division occurs?
123157.sol: In nuclear endosperm the primary endosperm nucleus divides repeatedly without wall formation producing a large number of free nuclei. It is most common type of endosperm.

123378.subject: Botany
123378.text: Terms Characteristics A. Cambium 1. Tissue between xylem and phloem B. Conjunctive Tissue 2. Tissue responsible for water and nutrient transport C. Xylem 3. Present between xylem and phloem in dicotyledonous plants D. Phloem 4. Tissue involved in the transport of food
123378.sol: Cambium is present between xylem and phloem in dicotyledonous plants. Conjunctive tissue is located between xylem and phloem. Xylem transports water and nutrients, while phloem transports food.

123652.subject: Botany
123652.text: What is the result of meiosis in plants and animals?
123652.sol: The production of offspring by sexual reproduction includes the fusion of two gametes, each with a complete haploid set of chromosomes. Gametes are formed from specialised diploid cells. This specialised kind of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half results in the production of haploid daughter cells. This kind of division is called meiosis. Meiosis ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms whereas fertilisation restores the diploid phase. We come

124021.subject: Botany
124021.text: Which face of the golgi apparatus do vesicles from the ER fuse with?
124021.sol: The golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell . Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum. A number of proteins synthesized by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the gol

124182.subject: Botany
124182.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Nucleolus and chromatin are in the nucleoplasm 2. Every cell has only one nucleus strictly 3. Contents of the nucleolus is continuous with the rest of nucleoplasm 4. Centrosome is the site of active RNA synthesis
124182.sol: The nuclear matrix or the nucleoplasm contains nucleolus and chromatin. The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of thenucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure.

124288.subject: Botany
124288.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The Golgi apparatus remains in close physical association with the endoplasmic reticulum. Reason (R): Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the trans face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the forming face. In the light of the above statements, choose the corr
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
124288.sol: The Golgi apparatus remains in close physical association with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to facilitate the transport of materials. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true. Reason (R) is false because materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face (forming face) of the Golgi apparatus, not the trans face. After fusing with the cis face, the materials are modified in the cisternae and move towards the maturing (trans) face, from where they are released. Thus, (A) is true but (R) is

124578.subject: Botany
124578.text: From which source was kinetin originally isolated?
124578.sol: Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Cytokinins have specific effects on cytokinesis, and were discovered as kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

124689.subject: Botany
124689.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. The Bakanae disease was caused by Gibberella fujikuroi 2. H.H cousins confirmed the release of ethylene from ripened oranges 3. Three researches coordinated and reported the purification and chemical characterisation of three different kinds of inhibitors: inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin. 4. F. Skoog and his co-workers observed that from the inte
124689.sol: The ‘bakanae’ (foolish seedling) disease of rice seedlings, was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi. H.H. Cousins (1910) confirmed the release of a volatile substance from ripened oranges that hastened the ripening of stored unripened bananas. Later this volatile substance was identified as ethylene, a gaseous PGR.

124712.subject: Botany
124712.text: A specific plant growth regulator is known to promote nutrient mobilisation and delay leaf senescence. Consider the following statements regarding this regulator: (A) It helps to overcome apical dominance. (B) It is synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs. (C) It promotes bolting in rosette plants. (D) It induces parthenocarpy in tomatoes. How many of the above statements are correct?
124712.sol: The plant growth regulator that promotes nutrient mobilisation and delays leaf senescence is Cytokinin. Statement (A) is correct: Cytokinins help to overcome apical dominance. Statement (B) is correct: Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, such as root apices, developing shoot buds, and young fruits. Statement (C) is incorrect: Gibberellins, not cytokinins, promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in rosette plants like beet and cabbages. Statement (D)

124807.subject: Botany
124807.text: What are labelled phases A, B and C in given sigmoidal growth curve? A B C
124807.sol: When a graph is plotted taking into consideration time on one hand and growth rate on the other hand, a 'S' shaped curve is obtained. It is called "grand period of growth". This total growth period is divided into three stages. (1) Initial lag phase (2) Middle log phase (3) Final stationary phase.

125111.subject: Botany
125111.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The whole of the respiration process in plants takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell. 2. Pyruvic acid is the key product of glycolysis. 3. There are four major ways in which different cells handle pyruvic acid produced by glycolysis. 4. Fermentation takes place under anaerobic conditions in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes.
125111.sol: In glycolysis, a chain of ten reactions, under the control of different enzymes, takes place to produce pyruvate from glucose. Pyruvic acid is the key product of glycolysis. There are three major ways in which different cells handle pyruvic acid produced by glycolysis. Fermentation takes place under anaerobic conditions in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes.

125346.subject: Botany
125346.text: What method is used to separate the leaf pigments?
125346.sol: Looking at plants have you ever wondered why and how there are so many shades of green in their leaves – even in the same plant? We can look for an answer to this question by trying to separate the leaf pigments of any green plant through paper chromatography. A chromatographic separation of the leaf pigments shows that the colour that we see in leaves is not due to a single pigment but due to four pigments: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue green in the chromatogram), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow

125709.subject: Botany
125709.sol: Light is the visible part of electromagnetic radiations. Sunlight or solar radiations reaching the earth have wavelength between (300 ~nm ) to (2600 ~nm ). Part of the spectrum used in photosynthesis has a wavelength between (400-700 ~nm ). It is called photosynthetically active radiation (PAR).

126245.subject: Botany
126245.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): On a mature seed, the hilum is seen as a distinct scar. Reason (R): It represents the point of attachment where the body of the developing ovule was fused with the funicle. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
126245.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because the hilum is a scar on the seed coat through which the developing seeds were attached to the fruit. Reason (R) is also correct and explains the assertion. In the ovule, the hilum is the junction between the ovule body and the funicle (stalk). After fertilization, as the ovule matures into a seed, this point of attachment remains as a distinct scar on the seed coat. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion. Answer: Both Asse

126400.subject: Botany
126400.text: Which one of the following generates new genetic combinations leading to variation?
126400.sol: Sexual reproduction generates new genetic recombination leading to variations. Advantages of sexual reproduction are more variation assists with survival. It increases the chance that at least some offspring of a parent survive.

126500.subject: Botany
126500.text: What is the effect of high temperatures on enzymes?
126500.sol: Enzymes generally function in a narrow range of temperature and pH (Figure 9.5). Each enzyme shows its highest activity at a particular temperature and pH called the optimum temperature and optimum pH. Activity declines both below and above the optimum value. Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat .

126591.subject: Botany
126591.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Enzymes and inorganic catalysts are different from each other. Reason: Inorganic catalysts work efficiently at high temperatures and high pressures, while enzymes get damaged at high temperatures and high pressure
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126591.sol: Enzyme catalysts differ from inorganic catalysts in many ways, but one major difference needs mention. Inorganic catalysts work efficiently at high temperatures and high pressures, while enzymes get damaged at high temperatures.

126682.subject: Botany
126682.text: Amino Acids have both an amino group and a carboxyl group in their structure. Which one of the following is an amino acid?

126759.subject: Botany
126759.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason. Assertion: All the elements present in a sample of Earth's crust are also present in a sample of living tissue. Reason: The relative abundance of carbon and hydrogen with respect to other elements is lower in any living organism than in Earth's crust. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from t
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
126759.sol: Assertion is correct: When elemental analysis is performed on a piece of Earth's crust and a living tissue, we obtain a similar list of elements. In absolute terms, all the elements present in a sample of Earth's crust are also present in a sample of living tissue. Reason is incorrect: A closer examination reveals that the relative abundance of carbon and hydrogen with respect to other elements is higher (not lower) in any living organism than in Earth's crust. Therefore, the Assertion is correct but the Reason is

127175.subject: Botany
127175.text: What is the main goal of a stable community?
options: To be resistant to disturbances and invasions by alien species
To have a high species richness
To understand the link between species richness and ecosystem health
127175.sol: A stable community should not show too much variation in productivity from year to year; it must be either resistant or resilient to occasional disturbances (natural or man-made), and it must also be resistant to invasions by alien species. We don’t know how these attributes are linked to species richness in a community, but David Tilman’s long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots provide some tentative answers. Tilman found that plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass.

127485.subject: Botany
127485.text: Which one of the following expanded forms of the following acronyms is correct?
options: IUCN - International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources
IPCC - International Panel for Climate Change
127485.sol: IUCN or IUCNNR (International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources) is now known as WCU (World Conservation Union). Its headquarters are at Morges, Switzerland. It studies the threat to biodiversity in all parts of the world by gathering information about the geographical distribution, population size and population changes of various taxa. It prepares a red list or red data book.

127796.subject: Botany
127796.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Net primary productivity of an ecosystem is always more than its gross primary productivity. Reason (R): A considerable amount of gross primary productivity is utilized by plants in respiration. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
127796.sol: Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilized by plants in respiration (R). Net primary productivity (NPP) is the gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (NPP = GPP - R). Because respiration loss (R) is a positive value, GPP is always greater than NPP. Therefore, the Assertion (A) is incorrect. The Reason (R) is a correct statement as plants do utilize a significant portion of GPP for their own respiration. An

127970.subject: Zoology
127970.text: Which part of the brain includes the olfactory lobes?
127970.sol: The system for control and coordination is highly evolved in the frog. It includes both neural system and endocrine glands. The chemical coordination of various organs of the body is achieved by hormones which are secreted by the endocrine glands. The prominent endocrine glands found in frog are pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal body, pancreatic islets, adrenals and gonads. The nervous system is organised into a central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), a peripheral nervous system (cranial and s

128118.subject: Zoology
128118.text: Which of the following specialised junctions performs the function of cementing to keep neighbouring cells together in animal tissues?
128118.sol: In animal tissues, adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells. Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic connections found in plant cells, not animal tissues. Answer: Adhering junctions

128355.subject: Zoology
128355.text: What is the function of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas?
128355.sol: Pancreas is a composite gland (Figure 19.1) which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland. The endocrine pancreas consists of ‘Islets of Langerhans’ . There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas representing only 1 to 2 per cent of the pancreatic tissue. The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called α-cells and β-cells. The α-cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the β-cells secrete insulin.Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called d

128574.subject: Zoology
128574.text: Hormones are called chemical signals that stimulate specific target tissues. Their action depends on the presence of receptors on the respective target tissues. Which of the following is the correct location of the receptors in the case of protein hormones?

129200.subject: Zoology
129200.text: Where are myelinated nerve fibres commonly found in the human body?
options: In the spinal and cranial nerves
In the retinas of the eyes
In the autonomic and somatic neural systems
129200.sol: Based on the number of axons and dendrites, neurons are divided into three types: multipolar (with one axon and two or more dendrites), bipolar (with one axon and one dendrite), and unipolar (cell body with one axon only).Nissl’s granules are granular bodies in the cell body of a neuron. They are composed of typical cell organelles and are also present in the dendrites. The synaptic knob is a bulb-like structure at the distal end of the axon of a neuron. It possesses synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters.

129223.subject: Zoology
129223.text: What is the purpose of a synaptic cleft?
options: To separate pre- and post-synaptic neurons
To increase the efficiency of impulse transmission
To regulate the release of neurotransmitters
To allow for direct current flow between neurons
129223.sol: The action potential is generated in response to a stimulus and travels along the length of the axon, transmitting the nerve impulse. The rise in permeability to Na⁺ is short-lived and is followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺. K⁺ diffuses outside the membrane, restoring the resting potential of the membrane.A synapse is a junction between two neurons that allows the transmission of a nerve impulse from one neuron to another At electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close

129261.subject: Zoology
129261.text: What does the medulla of the brain control?
options: Respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretions
Interconnect different regions of the brain
Regulate sexual behaviour and emotional reactions
129261.sol: The thalamus is a major coordinating center for sensory and motor signaling.The limbic system, along with the hypothalamus, is involved in the regulation of sexual behavior, expression of emotional reactions, and motivation.The amygdala, along with other structures of the limbic system, is involved in the expression of emotional reactions. The hippocampus, along with other structures of the limbic system, is involved in processing of memory and spatial navigation.The brain stem forms the connections between the bra

129697.subject: Zoology
129697.text: Read the following statements regarding the exchange of solutes in the counter current mechanism of the human kidney: (A) NaCl is transported by the ascending limb of Henle's loop which is exchanged with the descending limb of vasa recta. (B) NaCl is returned to the interstitium by the ascending portion of vasa recta. (C) Small amounts of urea enter the thin segment of the ascending limb of Henle's loop. (D) Urea is

Statement (B) is correct: This NaCl is then returned to the medullary interstitium by the ascending portion of the vasa recta, helping to build the osmotic gradient. Statement (C) is correct: Small amounts of urea diffuse into the thin segment of the ascending limb of Henle's loop from the interstitium. Statement (D

129798.subject: Zoology
129798.text: What is the main function of the conducting part of the respiratory system?
options: Humidification and regulation of body temperature
129798.sol: The outer pleural membrane is in close contact with the thoracic lining. whereas the inner pleural membrane is in contact with the lung surface. The part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitute the conducting part whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Exchange p

129939.subject: Zoology
129939.sol: The figure shows expiration or exhalation.

129964.subject: Zoology
129964.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Coelenterates exchange gases from their body surface Reason: Coelenterates exchange gases by simple diffusion
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
129964.sol: Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange O2 with CO2 by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.

130159.subject: Zoology
130159.text: What are cytoskeletal elements involved in amoeboid movement in cells?
130159.sol: Movement is one of the significant features of living beings.Streaming of protoplasm in the unicellular organisms like Amoeba is a simple form of movement.Movement of cilia, flagella and tentacles are shown by many organisms. Animals perform locomotion for the search of food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic conditions or to escape from enemies/predators. Some specialised cells in our body like macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement. Amoeboid movement in cells is

130198.subject: Zoology
130198.text: Are the thin filaments attached to the I-band?
130198.sol: .Skeletal muscles are known as voluntary muscles because their activities are under the voluntary control of the nervous system. The striated appearance of myofibrils is due to the distribution pattern of two important proteins - Actin and Myosin. The light bands contain actin and the dark bands contain myosin.The light bands in a myofibril contain actin and is called I-band or Isotropic bandThe actin filaments are thinner as compared to the myosin filaments. Hence, they are commonly referred to as thin filaments a

130522.subject: Zoology
130522.text: Total number of bones in the hindlimb of a man is
130522.sol: 1 femur +1 fibula +1 tibia +1 patella +7 tarsals +5 metatarsals +14 phalanges make one hind limb of man.

130637.subject: Zoology
130637.text: What does the given figure represent?
130637.sol: The given represents the condom for male.

130734.subject: Zoology
130734.text: What measures one has to take to prevent contracting STDs?
options: Blood transfusion from an infected person or drug abuser must be avoided
Sharing surgical instruments and injections needles must be totally avoided
Having sexual intercourse with an unknown person or multiple partners must be avoided
130734.sol: Blood transfusion from an infected person or drug abuser must be avoided. Sharing surgical instruments and injections needles must be totally avoided Having sexual intercourse with an unknown person or multiple partners must be avoided are some preventive measures you should take to avoid STDs.

130838.subject: Zoology
130838.text: What is the function of the penis?
options: To provide nutrition to germ cells
130838.sol: The penis is the male external genitalia. It is made up of special tissue that helps in erection of the penis to facilitate insemination . The enlarged end of penis called the glans penis is covered by a loose fold of skin called foreskin. The male accessory glands include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. Secretions of these glands constitute the seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes. The secretions of bulbourethral glands also helps in the lubrica

131094.subject: Zoology
131094.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa by the process called spermiogenesis 2. After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells, and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation. 3. Spermatogenesis starts by the end of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotrop
131094.sol: The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa by the process called spermiogenesis. After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells, and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation. permatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH). This, if you recall, is a hypothalamic hormone. The increased levels of GnRH then acts at the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secreti

131473.subject: Zoology
131473.text: What is the function of RNA in the synthesis of proteins?
options: Directly codes for the synthesis of proteins
Depends on DNA for synthesis of proteins
Synthesizes proteins without the help of DNA
131473.sol: Both DNA and RNA are able to mutate. In fact, RNA being unstable, mutates at a faster rate. Consequently, viruses having RNA genome and having shorter life span mutate and evolve faster. RNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins , hence can easily express the characters. DNA, however, is dependent on RNA for synthesis of proteins. The protein synthesizing machinery has evolved around RNA. The above discussion indicates that both RNA and DNA can function as genetic material, but DNA being more stable is pr

131477.subject: Zoology
131477.text: What is the role of RNA catalysts in living systems?
options: RNA catalysts catalyze important biochemical reactions
RNA catalysts are replaced by protein enzymes
RNA catalysts are not used in living systems
RNA catalysts are not important in living systems
131477.sol: RNA was the first genetic material. There is now enough evidence to suggest that essential life processes (such as metabolism, translation, splicing, etc.), evolved around RNA. RNA used to act as a genetic material as well as a catalyst (there are some important biochemical reactions in living systems that are catalyzed by RNA catalysts and not by protein enzymes). But, RNA being a catalyst was reactive and hence unstable. Therefore, DNA has evolved from RNA with chemical modifications that make it more stable. DNA

131967.text: In prokaryotes, genetic recombination can occur during

132597.sol: The given pedigree analysis is showing autosomal dominant trait. If such a trait is present in pedigree, it seldom skips a generation. An autosomal recessive trait may skip a generation. 133603.subject: Zoology
133603.text: Which of the following is not a character of cancerous cells in our body?
133603.sol: Normal cells show the property of contact inhibition, by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth. Cancer cells appears to have lost this property.

133762.sol: Once the BOD of sewage or waste water is reduced significantly, the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial ‘flocs’ are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge. A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum. The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. 134506.subject: Zoology
134506.text: How is recombinant DNA introduced into host cells in the method of biolistics or gene gun?
options: By allowing a disarmed pathogen to infect the cell
By injecting DNA directly into the nucleus
By bombarding cells with high velocity micro-particles
By incubating the cells with recombinant DNA on ice
134506.sol: This is not the only way to introduce alien DNA into host cells. In a method known as micro-injection, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell. In another method, suitable for plants, cells are bombarded with high velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA in a method known as biolistics or gene gun. And the last method uses ‘disarmed pathogen’ vectors, which when allowed to infect the cell, transfer the recombinant DNA into the host.

135136.subject: Zoology
135136.text: Can unrelated species compete for the same resource?
options: No, only related species can compete
Yes, unrelated species can also compete for the same resource
No, unrelated species do not compete at all
Yes, but only in aquatic environments
135136.sol: When Darwin spoke of the struggle for existence and survival of the fittest in nature, he was convinced that interspecific competition is a potent force in organic evolution. It is generally believed that competition occurs when closely related species compete for the same resources that are limiting, but this is not entirely true. 6a16f3247cfacf7984f866af.sol: Given acceleration a = 12t + 6 Velocity v = a dt = (12t + 6) dt = 6t^2 + 6t + C₁ Since the particle starts from rest, v = 0 at t = 0 , which gives C₁ = 0 . v = 6t^2 + 6t Displacement x = v dt = (6t^2 + 6t) dt = 2t^3 + 3t^2 + C₂ Since the particle starts from the origin, x = 0 at t = 0 , which gives C₂ = 0 . x = 2t^3 + 3t^2 At t = 2 s : v = 6(2)^2 + 6(2) = 24 + 12 = 36 m/s x = 2(2)^3 + 3(2)^2 = 16 + 12 = 28 m Ratio of displacement to velocity is x v = 28 36 = 7 9 Answer: 7 : 9

6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fa1.subject: Biology
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fa1.text: When three molecules of a hexose sugar ( C₆H₁₂O₆ ) are joined together by glycosidic bonds to form a trisaccharide, water molecules are eliminated during the condensation process. What will be the molecular formula of the resulting trisaccharide?
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fa1.sol: Three molecules of hexose sugar ( C₆H₁₂O₆ ) undergo condensation to form a trisaccharide. During the formation of a trisaccharide from three monosaccharides, two glycosidic bonds are formed. Each glycosidic bond formation results in the elimination of one water molecule ( H₂O ). Thus, two water molecules ( 2H₂O ) are eliminated in total. Total atoms before condensation: 3 C₆H₁₂O₆ = C₁₈H₃₆O₁₈ Atoms eliminated: 2 H₂O = H₄O₂ Molecular formula of the trisaccharide: C₁₈H₃₆O₁₈ - H₄O₂ = C₁₈H₃₂O₁₆ Answer: C₁₈H₃₂O₁₆

95290.sol: The cell wall of endodermis is deposited with suberin in the form of strips known as Casparin strips, which makes the layer impermeable. 95484.subject: Botany
95484.sol: The phylum Annelida typically has numerous segments, known as somites, and are covered with the locomotory structures called setae. The phylum Arthropoda has a body segmented into head thorax and abdomen. The body is covered by an exoskeleton that protects their organs and muscles.

95829.sol: Kingdom Fungi is divided into four classes depending upon the mode of spore and fruiting bodies formation and morphology of mycelium. These are class Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, and Deuteromycetes. Basidiomycetes are club fungi as they have a club-shaped organ known as a basidium. 96478.sol: In nature, the detritus food chain is connected with grazing food chains at some levels; some of the organisms of DFC are preys to the GFC animals, and in the natural ecosystem, some animals like cockroaches, crows, etc., are omnivores.

96482.subject: Botany
96482.text: By the process of leaching, _________ nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated.
96482.sol: Leaching is a process involved in decomposition. In this inorganic nutrients which are soluble in the water go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

96599.subject: Botany

96599.sol: As per the Ten percent energy transfer law introduced by Lindeman-'During the transfer of energy from organic food from one trophic level to the next, only about ten percent of the energy from organic matter is stored as flesh.' In a typical food chain, only ten percent of the energy is passed to the next consumer in the unidirectional manner and 90% is lost to the environment as heat. 96868.subject: Botany
96868.text: Which of the following types of roots are correctly matched with their examples? I. Apogeotropic roots: Rhizophora II. Absence of calyptra: Lemna III. Velamen containing roots: Vanda IV. Moniliform roots: Portulaca
96868.sol: Apogeotropic means negatively geotropic roots. They are seen in halophytes that grow in oxygen-deficient soil. So the root grows vertically upwards. They are also called pneumatophores. They are seen in Rhizophora, Sonneratia, Heritiera, etc. The Calyptra is a root cap. It is absent in hydrophytes that float on water such as Lemna, Pistia, etc. Velamen is hygroscopic roots found in epiphytes (plants which grow on large trees) such as Vanda . Moniliform roots are beaded roots found in Mimordica, Portulaca, etc.

97761.subject: Botany
97761.sol: The term glycolysis has originated from the Greek words, glycos for sugar and lysis for splitting. The scheme of glycolysis was given by Gustav Embden, Otto Meyerhof, and J. Parnas, and is often referred to as the EMP pathway. In anaerobic organisms, it is the only process in respiration. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell and is present in all living organisms. In this process, glucose undergoes partial oxidation to form two molecules of pyruvic acid.
